title: Demonstratives: This, That, These, Those
description: Point to objects near and far in both singular and plural forms with confidence.
objectives: Distinguish between near (this/these) and far (that/those) demonstratives
Correctly match singular (this/that) and plural (these/those) with appropriate nouns and verbs
Form questions and answers pointing to objects in everyday situations

vocabularyList.definition: Used to identify a specific person or thing close at hand.
Used to identify a specific person or thing at a distance.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: That is a very tall building over there.

vocabularyList.definition: Plural form of this, referring to items close at hand.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: These keys belong to my father.

vocabularyList.definition: Plural form of that, referring to items at a distance.
In, at, or to this place or position.
In, at, or to that place or position.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The pharmacy is right over there.
This picture on the wall is very old.

vocabularyList.definition: An opening in a wall fitted with glass.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Please close that window; it is windy.

vocabularyList.definition: A hinged, sliding, or revolving barrier.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Keep these doors unlocked during the day.

vocabularyList.definition: An electronic device for storing and processing data.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: That computer on the back desk is new.

sections.title: The 2x2 Grid of Demonstratives
sections.content:
Demonstratives point to specific things or people. In English, we choose the word based on **two factors**:
1. **Distance**: Is the item **near** (here) or **far** (there)?
2. **Number**: Is the item **singular** (one) or **plural** (two or more)?

tables.title: Pronunciation Guide for This vs. These

callouts.title: Pronoun vs. Determiner
callouts.text: Demonstratives can stand alone as pronouns (**This is great**) or attach to a noun as determiners (**This book is great**).

callouts.title: Never Mix Singular and Plural
callouts.text: Never say 'These book' or 'That books'. Match strictly: 'This book' (singular) and 'These books' (plural).

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: That = Singular, Far (That car over there).
These = Plural, Near (These keys in my hand).
Those = Plural, Far (Those birds in the sky).
Singular demonstratives take 'is'; plural demonstratives take 'are'.
